question: Muhammad Yunus, one of the pioneers in microfinance, founded Grameen Bank in which year?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1983 **__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Muhammad Yunus, a Bangladeshi social entrepreneur, economist, and civil society leader, founded Grameen Bank in 1983.
 
• He is widely regarded as one of the pioneers of microfinance and microcredit, concepts that aim to provide financial services to low-income individuals.
 
• Yunus was inspired to establish Grameen Bank after observing the struggles of poor villagers in Bangladesh who were trapped in cycles of poverty due to lack of access to credit.
 
• The bank was founded with the mission to provide small loans (microcredit) to the poor, particularly women, without requiring collateral.
 
• Grameen Bank operates on the principle that even small amounts of credit can help impoverished individuals start businesses and improve their livelihoods.
 
• The bank's model is based on trust and solidarity, with borrowers forming groups to support and guarantee each other's loans.
 
• By 2023, Grameen Bank had expanded its services to millions of borrowers, with a significant majority being women.
 
• The success of Grameen Bank has inspired similar microfinance institutions worldwide, contributing to the global microfinance movement.
 
• Muhammad Yunus and Grameen Bank were jointly awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2006 for their efforts to create economic and social development from below.
 
• The Nobel Committee recognized microcredit as a powerful tool to combat poverty and promote peace by empowering individuals.
 
• Yunus's work has demonstrated that access to financial services can transform lives and communities, breaking the cycle of poverty.
 
• Grameen Bank's repayment rates have been remarkably high, often exceeding 95%, challenging traditional banking assumptions about lending to the poor.
 
• The bank also offers other services, such as savings accounts, insurance, and housing loans, to further support its borrowers.
 
• Yunus's vision has influenced global policies and initiatives aimed at financial inclusion and poverty alleviation.
 
• Despite some criticisms and challenges, Grameen Bank remains a landmark institution in the field of social business and development.
 
• Muhammad Yunus has authored several books, including *Banker to the Poor*, which details his journey and the philosophy behind Grameen Bank.
 
• His work has earned him numerous international awards and recognition, solidifying his legacy as a global leader in social innovation.
 
• Grameen Bank's success has shown that poverty is not an insurmountable problem and that innovative solutions can create lasting change.
 
• The bank continues to operate as a symbol of hope and empowerment for millions of people worldwide.
 
• Muhammad Yunus's contributions have reshaped the way the world thinks about poverty, finance, and social entrepreneurship.
